description: SONAL WATERFALL Tucked away in the lush forests of South Goa lies a hidden gem that few tourists know about—Sonal Waterfall, located deep within the Netravali Wildlife Sanctuary. Far from the crowds and chaos of Goa’s beaches, this beautiful waterfall offers a peaceful escape into nature. With a thrilling forest trek, the sound of birdsong, and the cool splash of cascading water, Sonal Waterfall is the perfect destination for nature lovers, adventure seekers, and anyone who wants to explore Goa’s wild side. This blog takes you on a detailed journey to Sonal Waterfall—covering how to reach, what to expect, nearby spots, and tips for a perfect day in the lap of nature. 🌿 NETRAVALI WILDLIFE SANCTUARY -Location & significance: Situated in Sanguem Taluka of South Goa, Netravali Wildlife Sanctuary spans around 211 km². It forms a key corridor in the Western Ghats, neighboring other reserves like Cotigao and Bhagwan Mahavir. -Habitat: Thick moist-deciduous forests interspersed with evergreen pockets, peppered with perennial streams and ancient Myristica swamps 💦 WATERFALL TRIO: MAINAPI, SAVARI & SONAL -Local “gifts”: Neturli (or Netravali) village is home to three perennial waterfalls—Mainapi, Savari, and Sonal—all feeding into the Netravali River, a tributary of the Zuari. -Sonal Waterfall: -Hidden gem, lesser-known than Dudhsagar but spectacular in its own right . -Accessed via a 6 km trek starting from Netravali village, passing through tribal hamlets and dense forest. -Trail rated moderate: expect to cross streams, deal with leeches and mud (especially in monsoon), but reward is a stunning waterfall plunge pool 🦜 SONAL WATERFALL FLORA & FAUNA YOU MIGHT ENCOUNTER -Mammals: Gaur (Indian bison), Malabar giant squirrel, four-horned antelope, leopards, and black sloth bears roam the sanctuary. -Birds: Birdwatchers can spot Malayan night heron, Great pied hornbill, Nilgiri wood pigeon, grey-headed bulbul, and many more. -Butterflies: Look out for Malabar banded swallowtail, peacock, tree nymph, southern birdwing, blue nawab, black rajah, and redspot duke. -Unique amphibian: The Vulnerable Indirana salelkari (Netravali leaping frog) thrives in the splash zones of forest streams 🛖 SONAL WATERFALL CULTURAL TOUCH -Velip tribe: The Velip indigenous community inhabits Netravali. Their traditional beliefs and sacred groves—like sacred tanks and waterfalls—have played a vital role in preserving the ecosystem. SONAL WATERFALL TREKKING BASICS & BEST TIME TO VISIT -Trek details: Approx. 6 km one-way trek through dense forest, stream crossings, and interior wildlife zones. Prepare for wet, slippery conditions. -Monsoon magic: June to September brings roaring waterfalls, lush greens, and dramatic scenery—but also leeches and challenging footing. -Post-monsoon clarity: October to early February offers clear water, pleasant weather, and excellent birdwatching 📸 SONAL WATERFALL WHAT TO EXPECT ON TRAIL -Trail terrain: A journey across mud paths, stream crossings, occasional stream beds, and tribal huts . -Final stretch: The cascade forming a scenic plunge pool over mossy rocks; ideal for a cooling dip. “The waterfall is simply astounding. The cool water makes the trek uphill completely worth it.” 🧳 SONAL WATERFALL TIPS BEFORE YOU GO -Essentials: Good trek shoes, extra clothes, rain protection, drinking water, snacks. -Safety: Check for leeches, apply repellent. Avoid solo hiking—go with group or local guide. -Permissions: Entry permit may be required; nominal fee (~₹20‑30). -Guided treks: Look into local eco-trekking groups like Eco Treks or OffTrailAdventures. SONAL WATERFALL GOA Sonal Waterfall is one of the most beautiful hidden waterfalls in South Goa, located inside the Netravali Wildlife Sanctuary. It’s surrounded by dense green forests, chirping birds, and a peaceful atmosphere. Unlike popular tourist spots, Sonal Waterfall is perfect for those who want to enjoy nature in its purest form. The cool, fresh water, the sound of the falls, and the scenic trek to reach it make the experience unforgettable. If you’re planning to explore the wild side of Goa, Sonal Waterfall is a must-visit destination. NETRAVALI WATERFALL TREK The Netravali Waterfall Trek is an exciting journey through the heart of Goa’s wildlife sanctuary. The trek to Sonal Waterfall (and nearby Savari and Mainapi falls) is about 5 to 6 km and takes you through thick forest trails, tiny tribal villages, and clear jungle streams. It’s moderately difficult, so it's great for beginners and nature lovers. Monsoon and early winter are the best times to enjoy the full beauty of the waterfall. Don’t forget to wear good trekking shoes and carry some water and snacks! NETRAVALI WATERFALL The term Netravali Waterfall refers to the group of stunning waterfalls within the Netravali Wildlife Sanctuary—mainly Sonal, Savari, and Mainapi. These waterfalls are surrounded by untouched forests and are perfect for day trips, trekking, and nature photography. What makes these waterfalls special is their peaceful atmosphere—far away from the usual touristy chaos of Goa. If you’re in search of natural beauty, clean air, and refreshing waters, Netravali Waterfall will exceed your expectations. WATERFALL IN NETRAVALI Every waterfall in Netravali has its own charm. Sonal is known for its powerful fall and jungle surroundings. Savari offers a more relaxed setting with an easier trek, while Mainapi feels completely wild and untouched. These waterfalls are part of Goa’s eco-tourism efforts and are located in protected forest areas. Visiting them is not only a treat for your eyes but also a way to connect with Goa’s rich biodiversity and tribal culture. NETRAVALI WATERFALL IN GOA Netravali Waterfall in Goa is one of the state's most peaceful natural getaways. Located in South Goa, this group of waterfalls lies within a protected wildlife sanctuary that’s home to rare birds, butterflies, and animals like the Indian Gaur. What makes Netravali Waterfall stand out is the mix of adventure and calm—whether you want to trek, relax by the water, or just enjoy a forest walk, this place has it all. It's a great spot for eco-tourism and offbeat travel in Goa. NETRAVALI WATERFALL DISTANCE Wondering about the Netravali Waterfall distance? If you’re coming from Margao, it’s around 45 km, and from Panaji, it’s about 75 km. The nearest village is Netravali, and from there, you may need to trek about 5–6 km depending on which waterfall you're visiting. Sonal Waterfall is slightly deeper inside the forest, but the path is scenic and worth every step. It’s recommended to go by car or bike and to start your trek early in the day to return before sunset. 🌄 SONAL WATERFALL NEARBY ATTRACTIONS SAVARI WATERFALL -Located in the same forest zone as Sonal, Savari Waterfall is equally stunning and easily accessible through a trekking route. -It's a slightly easier trek compared to Sonal and perfect for a peaceful dip in the cool, clean waters. -Dense trees, chirping birds, and fresh air make the journey truly refreshing. MAINAPI WATERFALL -Just a short distance from Savari, Mainapi is another gorgeous waterfall hidden in the heart of the forest. -A little more adventurous to reach, but the natural pool at the bottom is worth the effort. -Best visited during monsoon or early winter when the waterfall is in full flow. BUDBUDYANCHI TALI (BUBBLE LAKE) -Located in Netravali village, this sacred lake is famous for its bubbling water surface—caused by natural gases. -Locals consider it a spiritual site, and the mystery of the bubbles makes it a fun stop for both kids and adults. -A calm, scenic place perfect for a quick rest and photo stop. GALGIBAGA BEACH (APPROX. 45 KM AWAY) -One of Goa’s cleanest and most peaceful beaches. -Known for being a nesting site for Olive Ridley turtles, it’s a serene spot with fewer tourists. -Ideal if you're combining forest and coast in your travel plan. BHAGWAN MAHAVIR WILDLIFE SANCTUARY & DUDHSAGAR WATERFALLS (ABOUT 60–70 KM AWAY) -If you’re up for more adventure, a trip to Dudhsagar Falls—one of India’s tallest waterfalls—is worth it. -It lies in the Bhagwan Mahavir Sanctuary and offers train rides, forest jeep safaris, and great photography opportunities. COTIGAO WILDLIFE SANCTUARY -Located south of Netravali, Cotigao is another serene forest reserve with tall trees, watchtowers, and chances to spot rare wildlife. -Less commercial, making it a great extension for wildlife and nature enthusiasts. 🚗 HOW TO REACH SONAL WATERFALL IN GOA Sonal Waterfall is located deep inside the Netravali Wildlife Sanctuary in South Goa, near the peaceful village of Netravali. Reaching this hidden gem requires a mix of road travel and a short trek through the forest. 📍 NEAREST MAJOR TOWNS: -Margao – approx. 45 km -Panaji – approx. 75 km -Canacona/Chaudi – approx. 35–40 km 🛣️ BY ROAD -From Margao - Take NH66 or the Margao–Quepem–Sanguem road. Head towards Netravali Village. The road is scenic and takes about 1.5–2 hours. -From Panaji - Drive south via NH66 → take the turn at Curchorem → head to Sanguem → then to Netravali. Takes around 2.5 hours. -From Canacona - Drive through Cotigao or via Betul–Quepem routes. It’s the shortest route to the sanctuary, around 1–1.5 hours. 🥾 TREK TO SONAL WATERFALL -Once you reach Netravali village or the forest checkpoint, you need to trek around 5–6 km to reach Sonal Waterfall. -The trek passes through thick forest, streams, and tribal paths. -It’s moderately difficult but safe if you wear good trekking shoes and go with a group or guide. 🚕 TRANSPORT TIPS -No direct public buses go to the waterfall. It’s best to hire a private cab, self-drive car, or two-wheeler. -Parking is available near the forest entry points. -Local guides are sometimes available at the base village or entry gate—recommended for first-time visitors.

headers.text: 🚗 HOW TO REACH SONAL WATERFALL IN GOA
headers.content: Sonal Waterfall is located deep inside the Netravali Wildlife Sanctuary in South Goa, near the peaceful village of Netravali. Reaching this hidden gem requires a mix of road travel and a short trek through the forest.
-Margao – approx. 45 km -Panaji – approx. 75 km -Canacona/Chaudi – approx. 35–40 km

-From Margao - Take NH66 or the Margao–Quepem–Sanguem road. Head towards Netravali Village. The road is scenic and takes about 1.5–2 hours. -From Panaji - Drive south via NH66 → take the turn at Curchorem → head to Sanguem → then to Netravali. Takes around 2.5 hours. -From Canacona - Drive through Cotigao or via Betul–Quepem routes. It’s the shortest route to the sanctuary, around 1–1.5 hours.

-Once you reach Netravali village or the forest checkpoint, you need to trek around 5–6 km to reach Sonal Waterfall. -The trek passes through thick forest, streams, and tribal paths. -It’s moderately difficult but safe if you wear good trekking shoes and go with a group or guide.

-No direct public buses go to the waterfall. It’s best to hire a private cab, self-drive car, or two-wheeler. -Parking is available near the forest entry points. -Local guides are sometimes available at the base village or entry gate—recommended for first-time visitors.

Wear proper footwear:➤ Use trekking shoes or strong sandals as the trail is slippery, muddy, and uneven.
Carry drinking water:➤ There are no shops nearby, so carry enough water to stay hydrated during the trek.
Avoid plastic:➤ Do not carry or throw plastic bottles, wrappers, or bags. Keep the forest clean.
Go with a group or guide:➤ It’s safer to go with locals or friends as the route passes through dense forest.
Start early:➤ Begin your trek in the morning so you can return before sunset.
Protect yourself from leeches:➤ Especially during monsoon, apply salt or oil to your shoes and legs to avoid leech bites.
Carry a small backpack:➤ Keep your hands free while trekking. Pack light with essentials only.
Respect local culture:➤ You may pass tribal villages—be polite and avoid disturbing locals or animals.
Check weather forecast:➤ Avoid visiting during very heavy rains or storm warnings as the trail becomes risky.
Don’t take unnecessary risks:➤ Don’t try to climb slippery rocks or jump into unknown water depths.

Where is Sonal Waterfall located?

Sonal Waterfall is located inside the Netravali Wildlife Sanctuary in South Goa, near Netravali village in Sanguem Taluka. It is surrounded by thick forest and is one of the most beautiful offbeat waterfalls in Goa.

How do I reach Sonal Waterfall?

To reach Sonal Waterfall, you must first drive to Netravali village by private vehicle (as public transport is limited). From there, you need to trek about 5–6 km through forest trails to reach the waterfall. The trek is moderate and takes around 1.5 to 2 hours.

What is the best time to visit Sonal Waterfall?

The best time to visit Sonal Waterfall is during or just after the monsoon season, from July to December. During this time, the waterfall is in full flow and the forest looks lush and green. Avoid visiting during heavy rains or the peak summer months.

Is Sonal Waterfall safe for swimming?

Yes, there is a natural pool at the base of the waterfall that is usually safe for swimming. However, it is important to be cautious during the monsoon, as the water current can be strong. Always check the depth and avoid risky spots.

Do I need permission or a guide to visit Sonal Waterfall?

In most cases, no special permission is required, but there may be a small entry fee at the Netravali forest gate. Hiring a local guide is highly recommended, especially if you’re visiting for the first time, as the trails can be confusing and the area is remote.

With a thrilling forest trek, the sound of birdsong, and the cool splash of cascading water, Sonal Waterfall is the perfect destination for nature lovers, adventure seekers, and anyone who wants to explore Goa’s wild side. This blog takes you on a detailed journey to Sonal Waterfall—covering how to reach, what to expect, nearby spots, and tips for a perfect day in the lap of nature.

-Location & significance: Situated in Sanguem Taluka of South Goa, Netravali Wildlife Sanctuary spans around 211 km². It forms a key corridor in the Western Ghats, neighboring other reserves like Cotigao and Bhagwan Mahavir.
-Habitat: Thick moist-deciduous forests interspersed with evergreen pockets, peppered with perennial streams and ancient Myristica swamps
-Local “gifts”: Neturli (or Netravali) village is home to three perennial waterfalls—Mainapi, Savari, and Sonal—all feeding into the Netravali River, a tributary of the Zuari.
-Hidden gem, lesser-known than Dudhsagar but spectacular in its own right .
-Accessed via a 6 km trek starting from Netravali village, passing through tribal hamlets and dense forest.
-Trail rated moderate: expect to cross streams, deal with leeches and mud (especially in monsoon), but reward is a stunning waterfall plunge pool
-Mammals: Gaur (Indian bison), Malabar giant squirrel, four-horned antelope, leopards, and black sloth bears roam the sanctuary.
-Birds: Birdwatchers can spot Malayan night heron, Great pied hornbill, Nilgiri wood pigeon, grey-headed bulbul, and many more.
-Butterflies: Look out for Malabar banded swallowtail, peacock, tree nymph, southern birdwing, blue nawab, black rajah, and redspot duke.
-Unique amphibian: The Vulnerable Indirana salelkari (Netravali leaping frog) thrives in the splash zones of forest streams
-Velip tribe: The Velip indigenous community inhabits Netravali. Their traditional beliefs and sacred groves—like sacred tanks and waterfalls—have played a vital role in preserving the ecosystem.
-Trek details: Approx. 6 km one-way trek through dense forest, stream crossings, and interior wildlife zones. Prepare for wet, slippery conditions.
-Monsoon magic: June to September brings roaring waterfalls, lush greens, and dramatic scenery—but also leeches and challenging footing.
-Post-monsoon clarity: October to early February offers clear water, pleasant weather, and excellent birdwatching
-Trail terrain: A journey across mud paths, stream crossings, occasional stream beds, and tribal huts .
-Final stretch: The cascade forming a scenic plunge pool over mossy rocks; ideal for a cooling dip.
-Essentials: Good trek shoes, extra clothes, rain protection, drinking water, snacks.
-Safety: Check for leeches, apply repellent. Avoid solo hiking—go with group or local guide.
-Permissions: Entry permit may be required; nominal fee (~₹20‑30).
-Guided treks: Look into local eco-trekking groups like Eco Treks or OffTrailAdventures.

Sonal Waterfall is one of the most beautiful hidden waterfalls in South Goa, located inside the Netravali Wildlife Sanctuary. It’s surrounded by dense green forests, chirping birds, and a peaceful atmosphere. Unlike popular tourist spots, Sonal Waterfall is perfect for those who want to enjoy nature in its purest form. The cool, fresh water, the sound of the falls, and the scenic trek to reach it make the experience unforgettable. If you’re planning to explore the wild side of Goa, Sonal Waterfall is a must-visit destination.

The Netravali Waterfall Trek is an exciting journey through the heart of Goa’s wildlife sanctuary. The trek to Sonal Waterfall (and nearby Savari and Mainapi falls) is about 5 to 6 km and takes you through thick forest trails, tiny tribal villages, and clear jungle streams. It’s moderately difficult, so it's great for beginners and nature lovers. Monsoon and early winter are the best times to enjoy the full beauty of the waterfall. Don’t forget to wear good trekking shoes and carry some water and snacks!

The term Netravali Waterfall refers to the group of stunning waterfalls within the Netravali Wildlife Sanctuary—mainly Sonal, Savari, and Mainapi. These waterfalls are surrounded by untouched forests and are perfect for day trips, trekking, and nature photography. What makes these waterfalls special is their peaceful atmosphere—far away from the usual touristy chaos of Goa. If you’re in search of natural beauty, clean air, and refreshing waters, Netravali Waterfall will exceed your expectations.

Every waterfall in Netravali has its own charm. Sonal is known for its powerful fall and jungle surroundings. Savari offers a more relaxed setting with an easier trek, while Mainapi feels completely wild and untouched. These waterfalls are part of Goa’s eco-tourism efforts and are located in protected forest areas. Visiting them is not only a treat for your eyes but also a way to connect with Goa’s rich biodiversity and tribal culture.

Netravali Waterfall in Goa is one of the state's most peaceful natural getaways. Located in South Goa, this group of waterfalls lies within a protected wildlife sanctuary that’s home to rare birds, butterflies, and animals like the Indian Gaur. What makes Netravali Waterfall stand out is the mix of adventure and calm—whether you want to trek, relax by the water, or just enjoy a forest walk, this place has it all. It's a great spot for eco-tourism and offbeat travel in Goa.

Wondering about the Netravali Waterfall distance? If you’re coming from Margao, it’s around 45 km, and from Panaji, it’s about 75 km. The nearest village is Netravali, and from there, you may need to trek about 5–6 km depending on which waterfall you're visiting. Sonal Waterfall is slightly deeper inside the forest, but the path is scenic and worth every step. It’s recommended to go by car or bike and to start your trek early in the day to return before sunset.

Sonal Waterfall is located deep inside the Netravali Wildlife Sanctuary in South Goa, near the peaceful village of Netravali. Reaching this hidden gem requires a mix of road travel and a short trek through the forest.
-Margao – approx. 45 km
-Panaji – approx. 75 km
-Canacona/Chaudi – approx. 35–40 km
- Take NH66 or the Margao–Quepem–Sanguem road. Head towards Netravali Village. The road is scenic and takes about 1.5–2 hours.
- Drive south via NH66 → take the turn at Curchorem → head to Sanguem → then to Netravali. Takes around 2.5 hours.
- Drive through Cotigao or via Betul–Quepem routes. It’s the shortest route to the sanctuary, around 1–1.5 hours.
-Once you reach Netravali village or the forest checkpoint, you need to trek around 5–6 km to reach Sonal Waterfall.
-The trek passes through thick forest, streams, and tribal paths.
-It’s moderately difficult but safe if you wear good trekking shoes and go with a group or guide.
-No direct public buses go to the waterfall. It’s best to hire a private cab, self-drive car, or two-wheeler.
-Parking is available near the forest entry points.
-Local guides are sometimes available at the base village or entry gate—recommended for first-time visitors.

Sonal Waterfall is located inside the Netravali Wildlife Sanctuary in South Goa, near Netravali village in Sanguem Taluka. It is surrounded by thick forest and is one of the most beautiful offbeat waterfalls in Goa.

To reach Sonal Waterfall, you must first drive to Netravali village by private vehicle (as public transport is limited). From there, you need to trek about 5–6 km through forest trails to reach the waterfall. The trek is moderate and takes around 1.5 to 2 hours.

The best time to visit Sonal Waterfall is during or just after the monsoon season, from July to December. During this time, the waterfall is in full flow and the forest looks lush and green. Avoid visiting during heavy rains or the peak summer months.

Yes, there is a natural pool at the base of the waterfall that is usually safe for swimming. However, it is important to be cautious during the monsoon, as the water current can be strong. Always check the depth and avoid risky spots.

In most cases, no special permission is required, but there may be a small entry fee at the Netravali forest gate. Hiring a local guide is highly recommended, especially if you’re visiting for the first time, as the trails can be confusing and the area is remote.
